paper.title: Regret Lower Bound and Optimal Algorithm in Finite Stochastic Partial Monitoring

unmapped: N actions (K=N), M outcomes, A feedback symbols; loss matrix L and feedback matrix H known to the learner
outcomes drawn i.i.d. from an unknown opponent strategy p* in the M-simplex; losses are deterministic functions of action and outcome and are unobserved
settings.definition_quote: This paper studies the finite stochastic partial monitoring problem with $N$ actions, $M$ outcomes, and $A$ symbols. An instance of the partial monitoring game is defined by a loss matrix $L$ and a feedback matrix $H$... At the beginning, the learner is informed of $L$ and $H$... The outcome $j(t)$ of each round is an i.i.d. sample from $\pst$. ... Assume that $\ist$ is unique. ... In this paper, we exclusively deal with globally observable instances

settings.name_in_paper: N-armed Bernoulli bandit represented as partial monitoring
unmapped: means assumed in (0,1) and pairwise distinct
settings.definition_quote: More generally, $N$-armed Bernoulli bandit is represented as an instance of partial monitoring in which the loss and feedback matrices are the same $N \times 2^N$ matrix ... For the ease of analysis, we assume $\{\mu_i\}$ are in $(0,1)$ and different from each other.

symbols.C_1_star: C_1^*(p^*,{p_i^*}): value of the LSIP min sum_{i != 1} r_i Delta_i s.t. inf_{q in cl(C_1^c), S_1 q = p_1^*} sum_i r_i D(S_i p^* || S_i q) >= 1

conditions: strongly consistent algorithm: E[Regret(T)] = o(T^a) for all a>0 and all p

source.label: thm:regretlower
source.quote: The regret of a strongly consistent algorithm is lower bounded as: \E[\regret(T)]\ge \optcone{1}(p^*,\{p_i^*\}) \log T -\so(\log T).

results.notes: Builds on Lemma 1 (lower bound on expected numbers of observations). Paper shows C_1^* = O(N/||p*-C_1^c||_M^2) in Lemma 5.

symbols.C_1_star: C_1^*(p^*,{p_i^*}): optimal value of the regret lower-bound LSIP (same as Theorem 2)

conditions: regularity condition 1: optimal solution set R_1^*(p,{p_i,delta_i}) is unique at p=p*, p_i=S_i p*, delta_i=0
regularity condition 2: cl(int(C_1^c) ∩ S_delta) = cl(cl(C_1^c) ∩ S_delta) for all delta >= 0 near 0

source.label: thm_main
source.quote: Assume the following regularity conditions hold for $p^*$. (1) $\optset{1}{p,\{p_i,\de_i\}}$ is unique at $p=p^*,p_i=S_i p^*,\,\de_i=0$. Moreover, (2) ... Then, \E[\regret(T)]\le \optc{1}{p^*,\{p^*_i\}} \log T +\so(\log T).

results.notes: Matches the lower bound of Theorem 2; asymptotic only (no finite-time analysis). Algorithm requires solving LSIPs, computational complexity not stated.

conditions: Bernoulli means in (0,1) and pairwise distinct

source.label: cor:bandit
source.quote: (Optimality in the $N$-armed bandit problem) In the $N$-armed Bernoulli bandit problem, the regularity conditions in Theorem \ref{thm_main} always hold. Moreover, the coefficient of the leading logarithmic term in the regret bound of the partial monitoring problem is equal to the bound given in Lai and Robbins. Namely, $\optcone{1}(p^*,\{p_i^*\}) = \sum_{i \neq 1}^N (\Delta_i/d(\mu_i \Vert \mu_1))$

results.notes: Combined with Theorem 3, gives E[Regret] <= sum Delta_i/kl(mu_i,mu_1) log T + o(log T) for PM-DMED-Hinge run on the Bernoulli bandit encoded as partial monitoring.
